# Langflow PR 13960 transaction fixture

This fixture uses source excerpts pinned to merge commit `a69a47ff1b5c99ce9c50edc4df45de4397151f17` (base `b40e4aa02661dcc9d630e1e97a0af45d45e88ae4`). `provenance.json` records the immutable upstream path and SHA-256 for each complete source file, SHA-256 for each excerpt, PR URL, and license. The excerpts are parsed as data by tests; tests never import or execute Langflow code.

The trace-clear route in `source/langflow/api/v1/traces.py` runs a bulk `DELETE` through `session.execute` inside the exact `langflow.services.deps.session_scope` context. That wrapper delegates to `lfx.services.deps.session_scope`. The pinned LFX implementation commits after a normal yield and rolls back an active session on both `HTTPException` and general exceptions. `effects.yaml` records this transaction context contract against the Langflow wrapper symbol. A normal context exit makes commit reachable; an exception makes rollback reachable. Neither establishes that a specific runtime path completed or that data is durable.

The trace-clear handler has no explicit `flush()` or savepoint. `source/langflow/api/v1/flows_flush.py` preserves the same PR snapshot's separate bulk-flow path where `db.flush()` is called before wrapper exit. The regression test excerpt records explicit seed and delete commits. Together the checked excerpts cover pending SQL work, flush, normal commit, exception rollback, and context exit. No `begin_nested()` occurs in the trace-clear operation; the existing synthetic transaction tests remain the savepoint control and verify that a configured nested context is classified as a savepoint. Runtime object identity and database durability are deliberately left unresolved.
